# Adjudication Task — Chapter 556

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃556화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|후우.
  6|
  7|한숨과 함께 주위를 훑었다.
  8|
  9|축축하고 서늘한 동굴 내부. 미로처럼 얽힌 좁은 통로와 천장에 매달린 뾰족한 종유석. 잔뜩 겁에 질린 피로한 얼굴들.
 10|
 11|‘그때랑 똑같군.’
 12|
 13|3년. 아니, 무림에서 보낸 시간까지 합한다면 4년 전이다.
 14|
 15|그날의 사고는 지울 수 없는 화인(火印)처럼 가슴에 남았고, 이미 복수를 끝마친 지금에도 완전히 잊지 못했다.
 16|
 17|“시벌, 옛날 생각나네.”
 18|
 19|텁텁하게 뇌까리는 나와 달리, 스켈레톤 킹은 흐뭇하게 웃어 보였다.
 20|
 21|“나 역시 마찬가지다. 이건 마치 너희가 말하는 고향에 돌아온 기분이군.”
 22|
 23|“…….”
 24|
 25|그거 아냐, 인마.
 26|
 27|서로 떠올리는 부분이 상당히 어긋나는 것 같은데.
 28|
 29|어쩌면 저놈이 내가 한창 하급 게이트를 전전하고 있을 때 마주친 스켈레톤 1이었을지도 모르겠다.
 30|
 31|그나저나…….
 32|
 33|구구구구궁!
 34|
 35|‘마력의 파동이 생각했던 것보다 훨씬 센데?’
 36|
 37|때마침 인근에 있었기에 망정이지, 하마터면 열심히 살아가는 생목숨이 스물이나 날아갈 뻔했다.
 38|
 39|나는 얼빠진 시선으로 이쪽을 응시하는 헌터들을 향해 손짓했다.
 40|
 41|“위험하니까 이쪽으로 오세요.”
 42|
 43|팀장으로 보이는 20대 후반의 남자가 눈을 깜빡였다.
 44|
 45|“뭐, 뭐요?”
 46|
 47|“오시라고. 빨리.”
 48|
 49|“그, 그쪽은 누구신데요?”
 50|
 51|어두컴컴한 동굴 내부. 상당한 거리를 두고 멀찍이 떨어진 내 얼굴까지 알아보기에는 저들의 수준이 너무 낮다.
 52|
 53|머쓱하게 턱을 긁적인 내가 입을 열었다.
 54|
 55|“저는…… 어어, 뒤 보세요.”
 56|
 57|“예?”
 58|
 59|반응이 느리다. 나는 대답 대신 손가락을 튕겼다.
 60|
 61|쉭, 퍼엉!
 62|
 63|미세한 파공음과 함께 녹색 핏물이 사방으로 튀었다. 동시에 어느 헌터의 등 뒤로 접근하던 고블린의 손에서 녹슨 도끼 한 자루가 힘없이 미끄러졌다.
 64|
 65|이어 머리통이 사라진 몸뚱어리가 썩은 통나무처럼 허물어진다.
 66|
 67|쿵!
 68|
 69|“헉!”
 70|
 71|“뒤! 뒤를 조심해라!”
 72|
 73|“뭐, 뭐야 이거.”
 74|
 75|뭐긴. 지풍(指風)이지.
 76|
 77|내심 중얼거린 나는, 황급히 재차 대열을 갖추는 헌터들을 보며 새삼 깨달았다.
 78|
 79|‘쟤들이 오는 것보다, 내가 가는 게 빠르겠구나.’
 80|
 81|하긴, 중간도 되지 않는 지점에서 고블린을 상대로 버벅거리는 걸 보니 하급 헌터인 것은 둘째치고, 그리 경험 많은 자들이 아니다.
 82|
 83|스켈레톤 킹이 금발을 쓸어올리며 진지한 표정을 지었다.
 84|
 85|“후, 이 몸이 나서야 할 때로군.”
 86|
 87|“가만히 있어. 깝치지 말고.”
 88|
 89|“…….”
 90|
 91|할 일이 정해지니 망설일 이유가 없다. 나는 그리 서두르지도, 그렇다고 느긋하지도 않은 걸음으로 그들을 향해 걸음을 옮겼다.
 92|
 93|저벅.
 94|
 95|한 걸음. 그리고 동시에 활짝 펼친 양손에서 뻗어나간 열 줄기의 지풍이 허공을 격하고 쏘아졌다.
 96|
 97|쉭, 퍼버버버벅!
 98|
 99|한 번 더.
100|
101|쉬쉬쉭!
102|
103|다시.
104|
105|퍼엉!
106|
107|우두머리쯤으로 보이는 홉 고블린을 마지막으로, 서른 마리에 달하는 고블린들이 머리 없는 사체가 되어 나뒹굴기까지는 찰나의 시간이면 충분했다.
108|
109|그리고…….
110|
111|저벅.
112|
113|세 번째이자 마지막 한 걸음과 함께, 어느 이름 모를 마법사가 라이트(Light) 마법으로 불러온 빛무리가 내 얼굴을 비췄다.
114|
115|화악.
116|
117|“……!”
118|
119|“……!”
120|
121|보이지 않는 충격과 동요가 동굴 내부를 휩쓸었다.
122|
123|모두가 넋 나간 시선으로 내 얼굴만을 바라보고 있던 그 순간, 막혀 있던 둑이 터지듯 비명 같은 외침이 곳곳에서 튀어나왔다.
124|
125|“시, 시벌좌!”
126|
127|“시부럴좌!”
128|
129|“지, 지, 지, 진태경!”
130|
131|그나마 마지막이 낫군.
132|
133|비록 이름이 여섯 글자로 길어지긴 했지만, 앞의 별명에 비하면 양반이다. 대충 이조참판 정도.
134|
135|그리고 어떻게 생각해 보면 현 상황에 딱 맞는 이름이기도 했다.
136|
137|점차 거세지던 진동이 어느덧 지, 지, 지, 지진으로 존나게 흔들리고 있었으니까.
138|
139|구구구구궁!
140|
141|설렁거리는 걸음으로 다가온 스켈레톤 킹이 머리 위로 떨어지는 종유석을 피하며 중얼거렸다.
142|
143|“이 정도로 요란한 걸 보니, 영 심상치 않은데.”
144|
145|“내 말이.”
146|
147|기껏해야 E급. 혹은 F급 정도인 이 게이트와는 하남에서 남만야수궁만큼의 거리가 있는 마력이다.
148|
149|작게 혀를 찬 나는 여전히 경악에 차 있는 헌터들을 향해 손짓했다.
150|
151|“아까 했던 말인데, 위험하니까 이쪽으로 오……”
152|
153|다다다다!
154|
155|“어잇. 깜짝아.”
156|
157|“언데드 맙소사.”
158|
159|뭐지, 블링크 마법인가.
160|
161|확실히 얼굴이 워낙 많이 팔리면 이런 장점이 있다.
162|
163|두메산골 김씨 할매도 내 이름 정도는 들어봤을 테니, 같은 업계인 헌터는 오죽할까.
164|
165|말이 떨어지기도 전에 빛의 속도로 뛰어온 스무 명의 헌터들이 두려움과 신뢰가 가득한 눈빛으로 나를 바라본다.
166|
167|“형님. 팬입니다. 진짜 팬이에요.”
168|
169|“꺅. 어떡해. 진짜 어떡해애.”
170|
171|“……고맙긴 한데, 다들 제정신이세요?”
172|
173|이 상황에서 저런 말이 잘도 나오는 모양이다. 황당함에 고개를 절레절레 흔든 나는 팀장을 찾았다.
174|
175|그나마 팀장답게 상황의 심각성을 제대로 파악했는지, 굳은 얼굴로 포켓을 뒤지던 그가 내게 뭔가를 건넸다.
176|
177|“사인 좀 부탁드립니다. 이승엽 헌터님 화이팅이라고 적어 주시면.”
178|
179|“…….”
180|
181|“부탁드립니다. 저희 집안 대대로 물려줄 가보로 삼겠습니다.”
182|
183|“…….”
184|
185|아. 씨바, 할 말을 잃었습니다.
186|
187|참담한 마음으로 브리핑용 보드판에 사인을 휘갈긴 내게, 팀장이 조심스럽게 덧붙였다.
188|
189|“그리고 실례가 안 된다면 욕 한 번만.”
190|
191|“예?”
192|
193|“욕이요. 소원입니다.”
194|
195|“……이 시벌 놈이.”
196|
197|“감사합니다. 감사합니다!”
198|
199|“진심이었는데요.”
200|
201|“헉.”
202|
203|그리고 그 모습을 심히 부러운 듯 바라보는 한 사람. 아니, 몬스터가 있었다.
204|
205|“인기가 제법이구나. 간악한 인간이여. 똥을 싸면 유명해지고 사람들이 박수를 쳐 준다더니.”
206|
207|“…….”
208|
209|뭔가 순서가 뒤바뀐 것 같은데. 공공장소에서 똥을 싸면 유명해지긴 하겠지만, 보통은 박수 대신 귀싸대기를 치지 않을까.
210|
211|하지만 스켈레톤 킹의 왜곡된 인식을 바로잡아줄 만큼 충분한 시간은 주어지지 않았다.
212|
213|내가 입을 떼려던 그 순간, 지진이라도 온 것처럼 흔들리던 동굴 내부에 급격한 움직임이 일어났기 때문이었다.
214|
215|구구구궁, 쩌저적!
216|
217|지면이 갈라지고, 천장에는 거미줄 같은 금이 쩍쩍 그어진다. 헌터 중 누군가가 신음처럼 중얼거렸다.
218|
219|“붕괴……?”
220|
221|반은 맞고, 반은 틀렸다.
222|
223|모두가 금방이라도 무너질듯한 천장을 바라보고 있을 때, 지면에서 벌어지는 일까지 파악하고 있던 나만은 그 사실을 알고 있었다.
224|
225|콰득, 콰드득.
226|
227|지면에 깔린 단단한 암석을 뚫고 고개를 내미는 새싹.
228|
229|검붉은 색을 띤 그것이 내가 바라보는 와중에도 무섭게 성장하고 있었다.
230|
231|가시를 만들고, 꽃봉오리를 터트리고, 그렇게 뿌려진 씨앗이 이내 사방으로 뻗어 나간다.
232|
233|콰드드드드득!
234|
235|“뭐, 뭐야!”
236|
237|“꺄아아악!”
238|
239|“으헉!”
240|
241|“잘라! 쳐 내!”
242|
243|이제야 그 사실을 눈치챈 헌터들이 황급히 움직였다.
244|
245|그러나 비명을 내지르고, 끝없이 뻗어 나가는 수풀을 무기로 내려쳐도 소용없다.
246|
247|당장 이 자리에서만 벌어지는 상황이 아니니까.
248|
249|아무리 나와 스켈레톤 킹이 나선다 해도, 이 짧은 시간 안에 게이트를 전부 돌며 저것들을 처리하는 것은 무리다.
250|
251|‘이건…….’
252|
253|단순한 붕괴가 아니다. 변화다.
254|
255|이 게이트 전체가, 새로운 형태로 탈바꿈하고 있는 것이다.
256|
257|‘말 그대로 변이(變異). 그 자체.’
258|
259|그렇게 사람들의 경악 어린 시선 속에서, 변이 게이트는 마지막 변화를 끝마치려 하고 있었다.
260|
261|쿠구구궁. 쿵!
262|
263|천장에 번진 실금이 진해지고, 틈새가 아가리를 벌렸다. 그 광경이 마치 동굴이라는 거대한 알이 깨지는 것 같았다.
264|
265|그리고…….
266|
267|쩌억!
268|
269|아무것도 존재하지 않아야 할 천장 너머로부터, 붉은색의 빛과 어스름한 안개에 휩싸인 무언가가 모습을 드러냈다.
270|
271|동굴과는 비교도 되지 않는 광활한 공간. 울창한 수풀과 습식 사우나처럼 후텁지근한 온도.
272|
273|“저건.”
274|
275|“미, 밀림?”
276|
277|충격으로 모두가 할말을 잃은 그때, 스켈레톤 킹이 나만 들을 수 있는 목소리로 속삭였다.
278|
279|“간악한 인간이여. 이 몸의 권능이 강해지고 있다.”
280|
281|비록 지금은 환영 마법으로 본 모습을 가리고 있지만, 스켈레톤 킹의 진정한 정체는 몬스터. 녀석의 힘이 강해졌다는 것은 즉, 한 가지를 의미했다.
282|
283|‘마력의 양과 밀도.’
284|
285|보이지 않는다. 그러나 느낄 수 있다.
286|
287|솨아아아.
288|
289|온 사방을 잠식한 강대한 마력을.
290|
291|금방이라도 터질 듯 팽창한 마력이 밀림을 짓누르고 있었다.
292|
293|이 정도면 A급 게이트에서도 쉽게 느끼기 힘든 수준의 마력이다. 평범한 하급 헌터들이 버틸 수 있을 리 만무했다.
294|
295|“흐읍. 흡.”
296|
297|“수, 숨이…….”
298|
299|서서히 풀려 가는 동공과 비틀거리는 신형.
300|
301|스무 명에 달하는 헌터 중, 단 한 사람의 예외도 없었다. 빠른 속도로 하나둘씩 혼절하는 그들을 가만히 지켜보는 내 모습에, 스켈레톤 킹이 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
302|
303|“간악한 인간이여. 너…….”
304|
305|“이게 나아.”
306|
307|“뭐?”
308|
309|“저 사람들이 깨어 있어 봤자 좋을 게 하나 없다고.”
310|
311|“……!”
312|
313|스켈레톤 킹의 존재는 최대한 숨겨야 한다. 그렇다면 생명의 지장이 없는 선에서, 처음부터 배제 시키는 게 낫다.
314|
315|목격자는 적을수록 좋으니까.
316|
317|털썩.
318|
319|마지막 한 사람마저 정신을 잃자, 내 눈짓에 고개를 끄덕인 스켈레톤 킹이 손가락을 튕겼다.
320|
321|콰드드득!
322|
323|어디서 솟아났는지 모를 무수한 뼈가 헌터들의 주위를 빈틈없이 감싼다. 스켈레톤 킹이 우쭐거리는 표정으로 말했다.
324|
325|“됐다. 이 몸이 친히 실력을 발휘했으니, 이것으로 저 인간들의 안전은 보장되었다.”
326|
327|작은 돔 형태를 이룬 그것을 유심히 바라본 내가 중얼거렸다.
328|
329|“글쎄. 좀 더 보강해야 할 것 같은데.”
330|
331|“쯧쯧. 간악하고도 불신에 가득 찬 인간이로군. 이 정도면 오우거 무리가 달려들어도 끄떡없을지어다.”
332|
333|오우거는 등급을 떠나, 무시무시한 근력만은 늘 최상위에 꼽히는 몬스터.
334|

[P70]
“Like I said, it’s dangerous, so come over—”

[P71]
*Patter-patter-patter-patter!*

[P72]
“Whoa. You startled me.”

[P73]
“Undead, have mercy.”

[P74]
What was that, a Blink spell?

[P75]
Being famous did have its advantages. Some old lady named Kim in the middle of nowhere had probably heard of me. Of course Hunters in the same line of work would know who I was.

[P76]
Before I could finish speaking, all twenty of them came running at the speed of light. They looked at me with fear and trust in their eyes.

[P77]
“Hyung. I’m a fan. A real fan.”

[P78]
“Eek! What do I do? What do I dooo?”

[P79]
“……Thanks, but are you all out of your minds?”

[P80]
How were they thinking about that at a time like this? I shook my head in disbelief and looked for the Team Leader.

[P81]
At least he seemed to understand how serious things were. His face was stiff as he rummaged through his pocket and held something out to me.

[P82]
“Could I get your autograph? Please write, ‘Go, Hunter Lee Seungyeop!’”

[P83]
“……”

[P84]
“Please. I’ll make it a family heirloom and pass it down for generations.”

[P85]
“……”

[P86]
Ah, fuck. I had no words.

[P87]
Feeling miserable, I scrawled my signature across the briefing board. The Team Leader cautiously added, “And if it wouldn’t be too much trouble, could you swear once?”

[P88]
“What?”

[P89]
“Swear at me. It’s my wish.”

[P90]
“……You fucking bastard.”

[P91]
“Thank you! Thank you!”

[P92]
“I meant it.”

[P93]
“Gasp.”

[P94]
One person—or rather, one monster—watched the exchange with obvious envy.

[P95]
“You are rather popular, wretched human. They say that if one defecates, one becomes famous and people applaud.”

[P96]
“……”

[P97]
He had that backward somehow. Taking a shit in public might make you famous, but wouldn’t people slap you instead of applauding?

[P98]
I didn’t have time to correct the Skeleton King’s distorted understanding. Just as I opened my mouth, the cave, already shaking like an earthquake had struck, lurched violently.

[P99]
*Rumble-rumble—crack!*

[P100]
The ground split, and cracks spread across the ceiling like a spiderweb. One of the Hunters groaned, “Is it collapsing…?”

[P101]
Half right. Half wrong.

[P102]
Everyone else was staring at the ceiling, which looked ready to come down at any moment. I was watching what was happening beneath our feet, too.

[P103]
*Crack. Crack-crack.*

[P104]
A sprout pushed its way through the solid rock covering the ground.

[P105]
Dark red. Even as I watched, it grew at a frightening pace.

[P106]
It produced thorns. A flower bud burst open, scattering seeds that soon began spreading in every direction.

[P107]
*Crack-crack-crack-crack!*

[P108]
“W-What is that?”

[P109]
“Eeeeeek!”

[P110]
“Ugh!”

[P111]
“Cut it! Chop it down!”

[P112]
The Hunters finally noticed and sprang into action. But screaming and hacking at the undergrowth did nothing to stop it from spreading.

[P113]
This wasn’t happening only here.

[P114]
Even if the Skeleton King and I stepped in, we couldn’t make it through the entire Gate and deal with all of it in so little time.

[P115]
*This is…*

[P116]
Not a simple collapse. A change.

[P117]
The entire Gate was taking on a new form.

[P118]
*Mutation. Literally.*

[P119]
Before everyone’s horrified eyes, the Mutated Gate neared the end of its transformation.

[P120]
*Rumble-rumble-rumble. Boom!*

[P121]
The hairline cracks in the ceiling deepened, and the gaps gaped open. It was as if the cave were a giant egg cracking apart.

[P122]
And then…

[P123]
*Crack!*

[P124]
Beyond the ceiling, where nothing should have existed, something appeared, wreathed in red light and dim mist.

[P125]
A vast space that dwarfed the cave. Dense vegetation. Heat as muggy as a wet sauna.

[P126]
“What is that?”

[P127]
“A-A jungle?”

[P128]
Everyone was struck speechless. The Skeleton King whispered so that only I could hear.

[P129]
“Wretched human. This body’s power is growing stronger.”

[P130]
Illusion magic hid his true appearance, but the Skeleton King was a monster. If his power was growing stronger, it meant one thing.

[P131]
*The amount and density of the magical power.*

[P132]
I couldn’t see it. But I could feel it.

[P133]
*Whoosh…*

[P134]
Immense magical power filled the air. It had swelled almost to bursting, pressing down on the jungle.

[P135]
Even in an A-rank Gate, it would be hard to find this much magical power. Ordinary low-level Hunters had no chance of enduring it.

[P136]
“Hhk. Hhk.”

[P137]
“I-I can’t… breathe…”

[P138]
Their pupils gradually lost focus, and they staggered. Not one of the twenty Hunters was spared. As they began passing out one by one, the Skeleton King frowned at me for standing by and watching.

[P139]
“Wretched human. You…”

[P140]
“This is better.”

[P141]
“What?”

[P142]
“Nothing good would come of them staying awake.”

[P143]
“……!”

[P144]
I had to keep the Skeleton King’s existence hidden as best I could. Better to take the Hunters out of the picture now, so long as their lives weren’t in danger.

[P145]
The fewer witnesses, the better.

[P146]
*Thud.*

[P147]
Once the last Hunter had lost consciousness, the Skeleton King nodded at my signal and snapped his fingers.

[P148]
*Crack-crack-crack!*

[P149]
Countless bones rose from somewhere and closed around the Hunters without leaving a gap. The Skeleton King looked smug.

[P150]
“There. This body has personally exercised its power. Those humans’ safety is assured.”

[P151]
I studied the small dome. “I don’t know. I think you should reinforce it.”

[P152]
“Tsk, tsk. Wretched human, you are distrustful indeed. This would hold firm even against a horde of ogres.”

[P153]
Whatever their rank, ogres were always among the strongest monsters in terms of sheer muscle. But the Skeleton King’s confidence didn’t change my mind.

[P154]
“It’d be fine against ogres. Those look a little different, though.”

[P155]
“Huh?”

[P156]
The Skeleton King turned to look. In the vast jungle, something was slowly rising to its feet.

[P157]
Twenty meters tall. Arms and legs longer and thicker than the countless giant trees around it.

[P158]
And…

[P159]
One enormous eye gazing down at the earth.

[P160]
A Cyclops.

[P161]
Mist shrouded the mythical giant from head to toe. Its single eye turned toward us, and an eerie voice boomed like thunder.

[P162]
—Intruders. Humans. Kill.

[P163]
And then—

[P164]
> **System**
>
> You have been forcibly moved to the Mutated Gate!
>
> An Unexpected Quest, **Forest of Giants**, has been created.

[P165]
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*

[P166]
The System notification rang in my ears as the jungle shook.

[P167]
No. It came alive.

[P168]
*Flap-flap!*

[P169]
Nameless birds shot into the sky. Beneath their beating wings, hundreds of trees rose with monstrous cries.

[P170]
Ancient tree spirits from countless tales. Ents awoke from their slumber and roared.

[P171]
—Gwoooooar!

[P172]
—Grrrrrrrr!

[P173]
One person—or rather, one monster—had watched it all in silence. He promptly changed his mind.

[P174]
“……I shall reinforce the humans’ barrier.”

[P175]
“Uh, yeah.”

[P176]
*Crack-crack.*

[P177]
Far more bones than before surged upward, piling on in layer after layer.

[P178]
The Skeleton King took care to finish the reinforcement, then fixed a grave stare on the advancing jungle.

[P179]
“Ready, Jin?”

[P180]
“Of course, King… Wait. Where the hell did you learn that?”

[P181]
“The internet. It is entertaining.”

[P182]
“You bastard. Once we get out of here, I’m confiscating your phone.”

[P183]
I muttered a threat at him, then spoke under my breath.

[P184]
“Inventory open. Summon.”

[P185]
At my command, the shaft of White Flame appeared in my empty hand. Its familiar feel was one I hadn’t known in a long time.

[P186]
I looked around at what had become a battlefield, and a smile touched my lips.

[P187]
*Let’s go.*

[P188]
*Whoosh.*

[P189]
Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi surged up from my lower dantian, became a fire dragon, and spread through every limb and bone in my body.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
